references.text: The Shema confession declares that the Lord is one, emphasizing the same monotheistic truth that there is no other God.
God himself declares that he is the only God and that there is no god beside him, paralleling the message in 4:39.
Solomon's prayer at the temple dedication expresses the same truth: that the Lord is God in heaven above and on earth below, and that there is no other.
Isaiah conveys God's word that he is the Lord and there is no other; there is no god besides him.
The Lord declares himself to be the first and the last, and that there is no god besides him.
God declares that he is God and there is no other; he is God and there is none like him.
Joel confirms that the Lord is in the midst of Israel and that he is their God, and there is no other.
Jesus quotes the Shema and affirms that the Lord our God is one Lord, and the scribe confirms that God is one and there is no other besides him.
Paul writes about one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all, emphasizing the unity of God.
Paul declares that there is one God and one mediator between God and mankind, confirming monotheism.
